judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Joint Resolution 3, which would have added the “Protect Missouri Voters” amendment to the Missouri Constitution. Its central change was that a constitutional amendment proposed by initiative petition would have passed only if a majority of voters in every congressional district approved it, on top of the statewide majority required today. It would have barred a committee that spends on statewide ballot measures from knowingly or willfully taking money from a foreign national or a foreign adversary. It would separately have barred any foreign national or foreign adversary from giving to or spending on such a measure at all. A violation would have been a crime carrying up to a year in jail, a fine, or both, prosecuted only by the Attorney General. It would have made petition signature fraud a crime. It would have required at least one public hearing after an initiative petition's signatures were filed and before the measure reached the ballot. It would also have required the full text of an initiative measure to be given to every voter with their ballot. The Missouri House passed it 98-58. It went to Missouri voters as Amendment 4 at the August 4, 2026 primary election, and they rejected it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1, which redrew Missouri's eight congressional districts in the middle of the decade, replacing the map the legislature adopted after the 2020 census. Under the act, the new boundaries first apply at the election of the 120th Congress, the November 2026 election. The act repeals the sections holding the previous map, writes the new districts into law county by county, and directs the revisor of statutes to publish the official map. The Missouri House passed it 90-65 and the governor signed it into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1, which redrew Missouri's eight congressional districts in the middle of the decade, replacing the map the legislature adopted after the 2020 census. Under the act, the new boundaries first apply at the election of the 120th Congress, the November 2026 election. The act leaves the earlier map on the books but limits it to elections through the 119th Congress, writes the new districts into law county by county and precinct by precinct, and directs the revisor of statutes to publish the official map. The Missouri Senate passed it 21-11 and the governor signed it into law.
